comment: The Ministry supports the position that centralised, federated, hybrid and virtual records are all valid expressions of the LHR capability. We note that dependence on a governed logical information model rises as implementations become more federated, not less: where data remain at source and are assembled on demand, there is no single repository in which structure can be enforced, so the comparability of the assembled record rests entirely on shared structural definitions. Readers may draw the opposite inference — that federation reduces the need for a common model — and the guidance would be strengthened by closing that gap explicitly.

Readers may draw the opposite inference — that federation reduces the need for a common model — and the guidance would be strengthened by closing that gap explicitly.
